```{r setup, include=FALSE}
extrafont::loadfonts(quiet = TRUE)

# ── Register EB Garamond with R's graphics device ────────────────────────
# CSS alone cannot reach text rendered into ggplot SVG/PNG output. We
# register EB Garamond with R's font registry so any
# `family = "EB Garamond"` ggplot/ggiraph call renders correctly.
#
# Two-tier strategy (both defensive, both no-op cleanly if unavailable):
#   1. systemfonts::register_variant — aliases "EB Garamond" to an
#      installed serif so R has metrics for layout. ggiraph still emits
#      font-family="EB Garamond" in the SVG and the browser pairs it
#      with the Google Fonts webfont loaded via www/cssloaders.html.
#   2. showtext (optional) — if installed, also pull the real Google
#      Font so static raster output looks correct.
local({
  if (requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
    have_eb <- "EB Garamond" %in% systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
    if (!have_eb) {
      candidates <- c("Garamond", "EB Garamond", "Georgia", "Times New Roman", "serif")
      installed  <- systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
      fallback   <- candidates[candidates %in% installed][1]
      if (!is.na(fallback)) {
        try(systemfonts::register_variant(
          name   = "EB Garamond",
          family = fallback
        ), silent = TRUE)
      }
    }
  }
  if (requireNamespace("showtext", quietly = TRUE) &&
      requireNamespace("sysfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
    if (!"EB Garamond" %in% sysfonts::font_families()) {
      try(sysfonts::font_add_google("EB Garamond", "EB Garamond"),
          silent = TRUE)
    }
    try({
      showtext::showtext_auto()
      showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = 96)
    }, silent = TRUE)
  }
})

# ── Self-contained download icon ─────────────────────────────────────
# Shiny's downloadButton() defaults to a Font Awesome glyph
# (<i class="fa fa-download">). When the FA webfont fails to load, that
# glyph renders as a blank tofu square. dl_icon() supplies an inline SVG
# instead, wrapped in an <i> tag so it passes Shiny's validateIcon()
# check (which requires the icon tag name to be "i"). This removes the
# webfont dependency entirely, so the download affordance always renders.
dl_icon <- function() {
  tags$i(
    class = "dl-svg-icon", `aria-hidden` = "true",
    HTML(paste0(
      '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" ',
      'width="1em" height="1em" focusable="false" ',
      'style="vertical-align:-0.125em;margin-right:0.45em;fill:currentColor;">',
      '<path d="M8 1.5a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v6.69l2.22-2.22a.75.75 0 1 1 ',
      '1.06 1.06l-3.5 3.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06 0l-3.5-3.5a.75.75 0 1 1 ',
      '1.06-1.06l2.22 2.22V2.25A.75.75 0 0 1 8 1.5Z"/>',
      '<path d="M2.5 10.75a.75.75 0 0 0-1.5 0v1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 0 2.75 ',
      '14.25h10.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 0 15 12.5v-1.75a.75.75 0 0 0-1.5 0v1.75a',
      '.25.25 0 0 1-.25.25H2.75a.25.25 0 0 1-.25-.25Z"/></svg>'
    ))
  )
}

east_coast_states_to_relocate <- c("RI", "DE", "DC", "MD")

us_states <- readRDS(here::here("data", "final", "us_states.Rds"))

#us_states <- states(cb = TRUE, resolution = "20m") %>%
  #shift_geometry() %>%
  #sf::st_cast("MULTIPOLYGON") %>% 
  #select(GEOID, ABBR = STUSPS, NAME, geometry)

us_states <- us_states %>% 
  left_join(
    us_states %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      bind_cols(
        us_states %>%
          sf::st_centroid() %>%
          sf::st_coordinates() %>% 
          as_tibble()
      )
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    x_lab = case_when(
      ABBR %in% east_coast_states_to_relocate ~ 2300000,
      ABBR == "FL" ~ X + 80000,
      ABBR == "LA" ~ X - 60000,
      .default = X
    ),
    y_lab = case_when(
      ABBR == "DC" ~ Y - 180000,
      ABBR == "DE" ~ Y + 100000,
      ABBR == "NH" ~ Y - 40000,
      ABBR == "VT" ~ Y + 40000,
      ABBR == "MD" ~ Y - 40000,
      ABBR == "LA" ~ Y + 40000,
      .default = Y
    )
  ) %>% 
  left_join(national_data)

### ----- Script sourcing helper -----
# Bare source() on a file missing from the deployment bundle fails with the
# opaque message "cannot open the connection", which says nothing about WHICH
# file is absent. On shinyapps.io that surfaces only as a stack trace in the
# logs. This helper checks first and names the offending path, along with the
# reason it is almost always missing: the file is not declared in the
# `resource_files:` block of this document's YAML header, so rsconnect never
# uploaded it. Run scripts/preflight_deploy.R before deploying to catch this
# locally instead of in production.
#
# `envir` must be an ENVIRONMENT, not TRUE/FALSE. Passing local = TRUE from
# inside this helper would evaluate the sourced file in the helper's own frame,
# and every object it defines would be discarded on return. Defaulting to
# parent.frame() reproduces what a top-level `source(..., local = TRUE)` does:
# evaluate in the caller's environment (here, the setup chunk).
source_required <- function(..., envir = parent.frame()) {
  path <- here::here(...)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop(
      "Required script not found: ", path, "\n",
      "  If the app works locally but fails after deploy, this file is ",
      "probably missing from the `resource_files:` list in the YAML header ",
      "of ADA_PARC.Rmd. Add it, then redeploy.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  source(path, local = envir)
}

### ----- Functions import -----

source_required("scripts", "functions.R")

### ----- Tier palette import -----
# scripts/palettes.R is the single source of truth for ADA-PARC tier colour.
# Sourced into the GLOBAL environment (envir = globalenv()) rather than locally,
# because ADA_PARC_PALETTE and the pal_* accessors are read from inside Shiny
# reactives and render functions that do not share this chunk's environment.
# Nothing below should carry a tier hex literal. See docs/color-palette-expansion.qmd.
source_required("scripts", "palettes.R", envir = globalenv())

### ----- Fixed city/place map classification -----
# City tract choropleth (output$snapshotmap) previously recomputed its color
# scale PER CITY (colorQuantile if >=4 tracts had data, else colorNumeric).
# That broke down for the many small/rural places with <4 tracts: 1-3 tract
# cities either got a non-4-step legend (colorNumeric + addLegend's default
# pretty()-based binning) or, for single-tract places, a blank legend (the
# domain collapses to one value, so addLegend's auto-computed cuts have
# length <= 1). See project memory "City Map Small-N Legend Bug".
#
# Fix: compute ONE fixed 4-category classification from the full national
# tract distribution (reusing the same create_non_overlapping_buckets() /
# format_ranges() helpers already used for the national state map), so every
# city's map is classified against the same breakpoints regardless of how
# many tracts that city has. This also makes colors comparable across
# different cities' maps, which per-city quantiles never allowed.
city_map_breaks <- create_non_overlapping_buckets(tracts_data$pct_cni_total_dis_place)
city_map_labels <- format_ranges(city_map_breaks, "pct_cni_total_dis_place")
```

# Home

```{r home}
# Embed logo as base64 data URI so the src resolves independently of Shiny's
# session URL context (relative paths like "PARC_blue_icon.png" can 404 when
# the browser resolves them against /session/ID/... rather than the app root).
#
# BRAND (provisional, 2026-08-04): www/brand holds the new identity pending
# approval from the ADA centers. Two blue-on-transparent files pair with two
# white-on-transparent files for dark surfaces:
#   PARC_blue_icon.png  / PARC_white_icon.png  384x384 square mark
#   PARC_blue_text.png  / PARC_white_text.png  448x264 two-line wordmark
# The hero carries both marks, mirroring the fact sheet banner adopted
# 2026-08-04 (fs_header() in factsheets/_generate/R/factsheet-functions.R):
# icon left, title block centred, wordmark right. The hero previously used the
# icon alone on the reasoning that the wordmark only repeats what the
# "Welcome to ADA-PARC" heading says; that was true of the words but not of
# the composition, and the home page and the fact sheets now open the same
# way. The BLUE files are used here, not the white ones, because the hero sits
# on the white page rather than on the navy banner.
logo_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(
  file = here::here("www", "brand", "PARC_blue_icon.png"),
  mime = "image/png"
)
wordmark_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(
  file = here::here("www", "brand", "PARC_blue_text.png"),
  mime = "image/png"
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* EB Garamond: declared here because shinyApp() sub-apps run in an
         isolated context where the parent flexdashboard www/styles.css
         does not reliably cascade into the rendered content. */
      *, *::before, *::after {
        box-sizing: border-box;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }
      /* ROOT FONT SIZE — read this before touching any rem value below.
         fluidPage() loads Bootstrap 3, whose scaffolding sets
         `html { font-size: 10px }`. Every rem on this page therefore
         resolved against a 10px root, which rendered 1.4rem body copy at
         14px and the contact line at 10.5px, roughly 62% of the intended
         size and well under the site's accessibility floor. Pinning the
         root here makes rem deterministic regardless of what Bootstrap
         version ships underneath, and every size below is expressed in
         rem against this 16px base (1.3125rem = 21px, matching the
         body size set in www/styles.css for the rest of the site). */
      html {
        font-size: 16px;
      }
      body, html {
        height: 100%;
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        overflow-x: hidden;
        /* `auto`, not `scroll`: `scroll` paints a permanent scrollbar track
           even when the content fits. */
        overflow-y: auto;
        background: #f5f7fa;
      }
      .main-content {
        padding: 2.5rem 2.75rem 3rem 2.75rem;
        width: 100%;
        max-width: 1020px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        background: #ffffff;
        border-left: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-right: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        min-height: 100vh;
      }

      /* ---- Hero ---- */
      /* Three-column grid, matching .factsheet-header: mark left, title block
         centred, wordmark right. `auto 1fr auto` is what makes the middle
         column centre against the PAGE rather than against the space left
         over between the two marks, provided the two side columns end up
         near enough the same width. They do: the 72px square icon and the
         wordmark set to 60px tall on a 448x264 file (~102px wide) differ by
         about 30px, which is not readable as an offset at this width. A flex
         row with `flex: 1` on the text block, which is what this replaced,
         cannot centre at all: it centres the text inside whatever width is
         left, so the heading drifts left as the wordmark grows. */
      .home-hero {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 1.5rem;
        padding: 1.25rem 0 1.125rem 0;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #7B1A1A;
        margin-bottom: 1.75rem;
      }
      .home-logo-wrap {
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      /* The brand icon is a 1:1 square, unlike the old wordmark it replaced,
         so height rather than width is the constraint that sets its visual
         weight. 72px reads level with the 32px hero heading; the old 96x64
         box would have shrunk a square mark to 64px and left it sitting
         light against the type. */
      .home-logo-wrap img {
        width: 72px;
        height: 72px;
        display: block;
      }
      /* Sized by HEIGHT, as on the fact sheet banner, so the two marks share
         an optical baseline. A width rule would set the height by accident,
         since the two files have different aspect ratios. */
      .home-wordmark {
        height: 60px;
        width: auto;
        display: block;
      }
      .hero-text-block {
        text-align: center;
        min-width: 0;
      }
      .welcome-text {
        font-size: 2rem;     /* 32px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.3rem 0;
        line-height: 1.15;
      }
      /* 19px, down from 20px. Below the 21px site body size, but this is a
         one-line standfirst under a 32px heading rather than reading copy,
         and it stays well clear of the 16px floor. #1c1c1c on #ffffff is
         17.4:1. */
      .welcome-sub {
        font-size: 1.1875rem; /* 19px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.4;
        margin: 0;
      }

      /* ---- Nav Cards ---- */
      /* Two columns, so four cards sit as a 2x2 block. Each card is wider
         than it was at three across, which is what lets the titles and
         descriptions carry the larger type without wrapping awkwardly. */
      .nav-cards {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
        gap: 1.125rem;
        margin-bottom: 2rem;
      }
      .nav-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-top: 4px solid #7B1A1A;
        border-radius: 0 0 6px 6px;
        padding: 1.375rem 1.375rem 1.25rem 1.375rem;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        /* Centred, matching the hero above. `align-items: center` is what
           centres the icon tile and the button, which are flex ITEMS and so
           are unaffected by text-align; text-align centres the title and the
           description, which are text inside full-width items. Both rules
           are needed, and neither substitutes for the other. */
        align-items: center;
        text-align: center;
        transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease, transform 0.15s ease;
      }
      .nav-card:hover {
        box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(123,26,26,0.12);
        transform: translateY(-2px);
      }
      /* Tile tint is #eef3fa, the palest usable step of the brand navy,
         replacing the maroon tint #fdf5f5 that paired with the old stroke.
         Not pure white: the card itself is white, so a white tile would
         erase the tile and leave the glyph floating. #eef3fa is 1.06:1
         against the card, enough to read as a shape, while the #013176
         stroke on it measures 11.07:1, comfortably past the 3:1 that
         non-text graphics require and past the 4.5:1 text floor as well. */
      .nav-card-icon {
        width: 50px;
        height: 50px;
        background: #eef3fa;
        border-radius: 8px;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        margin-bottom: 1rem;
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      .nav-card-icon svg {
        width: 26px;
        height: 26px;
        fill: none;
        stroke: #013176;
        stroke-width: 2;
        stroke-linecap: round;
        stroke-linejoin: round;
      }
      .nav-card-title {
        font-size: 1.3125rem;   /* 21px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
        line-height: 1.25;
      }
      .nav-card-desc {
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        flex-grow: 1;
      }
      /* Brand navy #013176, sampled from the tile fill of the PARC icon and
         defined as --brand-navy in factsheets/_generate/assets/factsheet-base.css.
         The jump-ahead buttons carry the identity colour rather than maroon so
         the one interactive element on the page is the one thing wearing the
         mark's blue; maroon stays on the structural rules (card top border,
         hero underline) and on the card icons. Hard-coded rather than
         referenced because this sub-app runs in an isolated shinyApp() context
         that the parent stylesheet's custom properties do not reach; if the
         approved brand shifts the blue, this literal and --brand-navy must
         move together.
         #ffffff on #013176 is 12.34:1. */
      .nav-card-btn {
        display: inline-block;
        padding: 0.55rem 1.2rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        background-color: #013176;
        border-radius: 4px;
        text-decoration: none !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.02em;
        transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
        cursor: pointer;
        border: none;
      }
      /* Gold on the darker blue is 6.6:1, so the hover state clears AA for
         normal text and does not depend on the 17px weight to pass. */
      .nav-card-btn:hover {
        background-color: #01214f;
        color: #C9A428 !important;
      }

      /* ---- Callout (full-width) ---- */
      .callout-full {
        border-left: 4px solid #7B1A1A;
        background: #f9f7f4;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 2rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .callout-label {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px, uppercase with tracking */
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: 0.1em;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        color: #7B1A1A;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
      }
      .callout-text {
        font-size: 1.1875rem;   /* 19px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        font-weight: 500;
        margin: 0;
      }

      /* ---- Single-column sections ---- */
      .home-section {
        padding-bottom: 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.5rem;
        border-bottom: 0.5px solid #e4e8ef;
      }
      .home-section:last-of-type {
        border-bottom: none;
        margin-bottom: 0;
        padding-bottom: 0;
      }
      .sec-heading {
        font-size: 1.5rem;      /* 24px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.6rem 0;
        line-height: 1.25;
        border-left: 3px solid #7B1A1A;
        padding-left: 0.7rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .sec-body {
        font-size: 1.1875rem;   /* 19px */
        color: #2d3748;
        line-height: 1.7;
        margin: 0;
      }
      .sec-sub {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-bottom: 0.6rem;
      }

      /* ---- Regions Grid ---- */
      .regions-grid {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
        gap: 0.2rem 2rem;
        margin: 0.75rem 0;
        list-style: none;
        padding: 0;
      }
      .regions-grid li {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        color: #2d3748;
        line-height: 1.55;
        padding: 4px 0;
      }
      .region-num {
        color: #7B1A1A;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-right: 5px;
      }

      /* ---- Bottom Bar ---- */
      .bottom-bar {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
        gap: 1.75rem;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1.5px solid #e0d6d6;
        border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 1.375rem 1.5rem;
        margin-top: 2rem;
      }
      .bottom-col-title {
        font-size: 1.25rem;     /* 20px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
        line-height: 1.25;
        border-left: 3px solid #7B1A1A;
        padding-left: 0.55rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .bottom-col-body {
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        color: #333333;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }
      /* Lead line of the authorship column, so the current maintainer reads
         as the primary credit and the historical contributors sit under it. */
      .bottom-col-lead {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }
      .bottom-col-note {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px */
        color: #333333;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-top: 0.2rem;
      }
      .bottom-col-body a {
        color: #7B1A1A;
        text-decoration: underline;
      }
      .email-button {
        display: inline-block;
        padding: 0.5rem 1.2rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        font-weight: 600;
        color: white !important;
        background-color: #7B1A1A;
        border-radius: 4px;
        text-decoration: none !important;
        margin: 0.6rem 0 0.5rem 0;
        letter-spacing: 0.02em;
        transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
      }
      .email-button:hover {
        background-color: #5e1414;
        text-decoration: none !important;
      }
      .questions-contact {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
      }

      /* Narrow desktop and tablet: keep the 2x2 card block until the cards
         would be too tight to hold a title on one line. */
      @media (max-width: 780px) {
        .main-content { padding: 2rem 1.75rem 2.5rem 1.75rem; }
        .nav-cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
        .bottom-bar { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
      }

      @media (max-width: 640px) {
        .main-content { padding: 1.5rem 1.25rem 2rem 1.25rem; }
        /* Stacked hero: the marks are grid items, not inline content, so
           text-align cannot centre them. justify-self can. */
        .home-hero { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0.85rem; text-align: center; }
        .home-logo-wrap, .home-wordmark { justify-self: center; }
        .regions-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
        .welcome-text { font-size: 1.75rem; }  /* 28px */
        .sec-heading { font-size: 1.3125rem; } /* 21px */
      }
    "))
  ),

  div(class = "main-content",

      # Hero
      # Icon carries alt="" because the wordmark to its right already names
      # the centre, and the heading names it a third time; announcing the
      # mark here would make a screen reader say "ADA-PARC" three times
      # before the first sentence of the page.
      div(class = "home-hero",
        div(class = "home-logo-wrap",
          tags$img(src = logo_uri, alt = "")
        ),
        div(class = "hero-text-block",
          div(class = "welcome-text", "Welcome to ADA-PARC"),
          div(class = "welcome-sub", "Tracking disability participation across the United States")
        ),
        tags$img(class = "home-wordmark", src = wordmark_uri, alt = "ADA-PARC")
      ),

      # Navigation script: from the Home nav cards, jump to a top-level
      # flexdashboard page.
      #
      # Home renders as an embedded shinyApp(), so this code runs inside an
      # iframe that does not contain the navbar. Three paths are tried in
      # order, each independent of the last:
      #
      #   1. Direct: reach top.document and drive the navbar link. Only
      #      possible when parent and frame share an origin; throws otherwise.
      #   2. postMessage: hand the request to the listener installed in
      #      www/cssloaders.html, which runs in the document that owns the
      #      navbar. Works regardless of origin. This is the path that was
      #      missing, and the reason the cards did nothing.
      #   3. Hash: last resort, same-origin only.
      #
      # Every selector is scoped to the top navbar (.navbar-nav), so inner
      # tabsets such as the Scorecards tabset, and the scorecard/factsheet
      # iframes, can never be targeted by mistake.
      tags$script(HTML("
window.adaparcNavigateToTab = function(page) {
  var slugs = {
    'Home':          'home',
    'National Data': 'national-data',
    'City Data':     'city-data',
    'Scorecards':    'scorecards',
    'Scorecard':     'scorecards',
    'Fact Sheets':   'fact-sheets',
    'Help':          'help'
  };
  var slug = slugs[page];

  /* 1) Same-origin direct path. Any cross-origin access throws, which is
        caught here so the postMessage path below still runs. */
  try {
    var doc = top.document;
    void doc.documentElement;
    if (typeof top.adaparcShowPage === 'function') {
      if (top.adaparcShowPage(page)) { return true; }
    }
    if (slug) {
      var byHref = doc.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav a[href$=\\'#' + slug + '\\']');
      if (byHref.length) { byHref[0].click(); return true; }
    }
    var links = doc.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav a');
    for (var i = 0; i < links.length; i++) {
      if ((links[i].textContent || '').trim() === page) { links[i].click(); return true; }
    }
  } catch (e) { /* fall through to postMessage */ }

  /* 2) Cross-origin safe path. The listener lives in www/cssloaders.html. */
  try {
    var target = (window.parent && window.parent !== window) ? window.parent : top;
    target.postMessage({ adaparc: 'navigate', page: page }, '*');
    return true;
  } catch (e) {}

  /* 3) Last resort. */
  if (slug) {
    try { top.location.hash = '#' + slug; return true; } catch (e) {}
  }
  return false;
};
      ")),

      # Navigation Cards
      div(class = "nav-cards",

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9 20L3 17V4l6 3m0 13l6-3m-6 3V7m6 10l6 3V7l-6-3m0 13V7M9 7l6-3"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "National Data"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "Examine national and state-level patterns for people with disabilities."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to National Data",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('National Data');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        ),

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="3" y="8" width="5" height="13"/><rect x="9.5" y="3" width="5" height="18"/><rect x="16" y="11" width="5" height="10"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "City Data"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "Investigate disability statistics at the municipal and city level."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to City Data",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('City Data');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        ),

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9 5H7a2 2 0 00-2 2v12a2 2 0 002 2h10a2 2 0 002-2V7a2 2 0 00-2-2h-2M9 5a2 2 0 002 2h2a2 2 0 002-2M9 5a2 2 0 012-2h2a2 2 0 012 2m-6 9l2 2 4-4"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "Scorecards"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "View state-by-state report cards across each disability domain."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to Scorecards",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('Scorecards');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        ),

        div(class = "nav-card",
          div(class = "nav-card-icon",
            HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M14 3H7a2 2 0 00-2 2v14a2 2 0 002 2h10a2 2 0 002-2V8l-5-5z"/><path d="M14 3v5h5"/><path d="M9 13h6M9 17h6"/></svg>')
          ),
          div(class = "nav-card-title", "Fact Sheets"),
          div(class = "nav-card-desc", "Read short, plain-language briefs on single disability outcomes."),
          tags$button(
            class = "nav-card-btn", type = "button",
            `aria-label` = "Navigate to Fact Sheets",
            onclick = "window.adaparcNavigateToTab('Fact Sheets');",
            HTML("Explore \u2192")
          )
        )

      ),

      # Did You Know callout \u2014 full width
      div(class = "callout-full",
        div(class = "callout-label", "Did you know"),
        tags$p(class = "callout-text",
          "Nationally, between the ages of 18 to 64, 1 in 4 individuals with a disability live below the poverty line."
        )
      ),

      # Single-column sections
      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "What is the ADA?"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), established in 1990, is a landmark civil rights law that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life.",
          " Since the ADA, organizations across public and private sectors have worked to improve the quality of life for individuals with disabilities in the U.S. ADA-PARC emphasizes key components of Census and HUD data to shed light on the lived experiences and outcomes for people with disabilities."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "Work of the ADA-PARC"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The ADA-PARC has research teams focused on Community Living, Community Participation, and Work/Economic Participation measures, using Regional Steering Committees in each of the ten participating regions to gather and review appropriate data.",
          " The intent of this effort is to inform ADA Center technical assistance and to help community-level stakeholders increase participation opportunities in their communities."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "About the ADA-PARC"),
        div(class = "sec-sub",
          "A collaborative research project of ten ADA Regional Centers:"
        ),
        tags$ul(
          class = "regions-grid",
          role = "list",
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">1.</span> New England')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">2.</span> Northeast')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">3.</span> Mid-Atlantic')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">4.</span> Southeast')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">5.</span> Great Lakes')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">6.</span> Southwest')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">7.</span> Great Plains')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">8.</span> Rocky Mountain')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">9.</span> Pacific')),
          tags$li(HTML('<span class="region-num">10.</span> Northwest'))
        ),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "Collaborating institutions include the ADA Knowledge Translation Center, TIRR Memorial Hermann, Syracuse University, and the University of Illinois at Chicago."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "Purpose of this website"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The ADA-PARC website presents public data that illuminates the status of people with disabilities in local communities, including national, state, county, and city data.",
          " The three main data domains are Community Living, Community Participation, and Work & Economics, each presented in map and tabular form."
        )
      ),

      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "Grant Information"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
```

# National Data

```{r National Data}
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(shinycssloaders)
library(DT)
library(ggiraph)

# Pre-compute initial topic choices so the selector has a valid value on load
.initial_nat_choices <- dict_vars %>%
  filter(is_demographics == TRUE, !is.na(national_dropdown_label)) %>%
  select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable) %>%
  tibble::deframe() %>%
  names()
.initial_nat_selected <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% .initial_nat_choices) {
  "People with Disabilities"
} else {
  .initial_nat_choices[1]
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* TABLE CONTAINER */
      .table-container {
        height: auto;
        max-height: none;
        min-height: 500px;
        overflow-y: visible;
        margin-bottom: 40px;
      }
      .table-container .dataTables_wrapper .dataTables_scrollBody {
        height: auto !important;
        max-height: none !important;
        overflow-y: visible !important;
      }

      /* Add space between map legend and table controls */
      .table-container .dataTables_wrapper {
        margin-top: 1rem;
        clear: both;
      }

      /* NATIONAL TABLE STYLING
         Roomier on-screen table (the downloadable report keeps its own,
         tighter print styling in national/national_topic.qmd).
         Selectors are written as table.dataTable.table_national so they
         outrank DataTables' own thead/tbody padding rules; a bare
         .table_national th loses that cascade and the padding is dropped. */
      .table_national {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th {
        position: sticky;
        top: 0;
        background-color: #1c2b3a;
        color: #ffffff;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 19px;
        z-index: 1;
        white-space: normal;      /* allow wrapping */
        word-wrap: break-word;    /* wrap long words */
        /* Header row sits taller than the body rows: ~62px vs ~50px for a
           single line of text. Extra right padding keeps header labels clear
           of the sort arrows, which DataTables absolutely positions there. */
        padding: 18px 26px 18px 12px;
        line-height: 1.25;
        vertical-align: middle;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national tbody td {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        white-space: nowrap;
        /* ~36px body row against the ~62px header, scaled back from a first
           pass that ran too roomy. Header left as is, so it keeps reading as
           clearly taller than the body rows. */
        padding: 7px 12px;
        line-height: 1.3;
        vertical-align: middle;
      }

      /* Right-align numeric cells; left-align State */
      table.dataTable.table_national tbody td {
        text-align: right;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national tbody td:first-child {
        text-align: left;
      }

      /* Remove extra space under h1 */
      h1 {
        margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
      }

      /* Intro text under National Data */
      .national-intro {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
      }

      /* Map summary text */
      .map-summary {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* DataTables controls font */
      div.dataTables_wrapper,
      div.dataTables_wrapper label,
      div.dataTables_wrapper select,
      div.dataTables_wrapper input {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }

      /* Map / table section heading inside cards */
      .national-map-title {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 1.9rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-bottom: 0.65rem;
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
        padding-bottom: 0.4rem;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #6d1f2e;
      }

      /* Interpretation note under table title */
      .interpretation-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        color: #000000;
        font-style: normal;
        margin-top: -0.25rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
      }

      /* Standalone interpretation-note container shown above the map.
         Maroon accent + pale gold-tinted panel (design canon). Dark navy
         text on the pale panel keeps contrast well above WCAG AA at the
         17px minimum body size used across the site. */
      .map-interpretation-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        line-height: 1.5;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        background: #faf5ec;
        border: 1px solid #e6d9bd;
        border-left: 5px solid #6d1f2e;
        border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 0.7rem 1rem;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1rem 0;
      }
      .map-interpretation-note-label {
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #6d1f2e;
      }

      /* SelectInput controls styling */
      .shiny-input-container label {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-weight: 500;
      }
      select.form-control, .selectize-input {

        font-size: 18px !important;
      }

      .leaflet-control-layers-list label {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 16px !important;
      }
      .info {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 16px !important;
        padding: 10px 15px;
        background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.95);
        border-radius: 5px;

      }
      .info h4 {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;

        margin: 0 0 5px 0;
        font-weight: 600;
      }
      .legend {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 17px !important;
      }
      .legend label {
        display: block;
        margin-bottom: 5px;
      }

      /* Source note below table */
      .national-source-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 16px;
        color: #444;
        margin-top: 0.75rem;
        margin-bottom: 1rem;
      }

      /* ── National controls panel ─────────────────────────────────────────
         One horizontal band: the two selectors on the left, the download on
         the right behind a full-height vertical rule. The topic summary lives
         in its own card below so nothing competes for width here. */
      .national-controls-split {
        display: flex;
        align-items: stretch;
        gap: 1.5rem;
      }

      /* Selector row: align-items:flex-start keeps the two labels on the same
         baseline. Bottom alignment used to push the shorter control down

      .national-controls-row {

        flex-wrap: wrap;

        gap: 1.25rem;

        flex: 1 1 16rem;

      /* Shiny wraps selectInput in .form-group with a bottom margin; zeroing
         it lets align-items:flex-end line the controls up exactly. */
      .national-control-field .form-group {
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }
      /* The download occupies its own full-height column, set off by a rule

      .national-control-action {

        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        border-left: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
        padding-left: 1.5rem;
      }

      /* Download Selected Topic button */
      .btn-download-national {
        background: #6d1f2e !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #6d1f2e !important;
        border-radius: 6px !important;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 1.1rem !important;
        font-weight: 700 !important;
        padding: 9px 20px !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        line-height: 1.4 !important;
        display: inline-flex !important;
        align-items: center !important;
        white-space: normal !important;
        text-align: left !important;
      }
      .btn-download-national:hover {
        background: #8b2737 !important;
        border-color: #8b2737 !important;
      }
      .btn-download-national:focus {
        outline: 3px solid #c9a84c !important;
        outline-offset: 2px !important;
      }
      /* Narrow screens: stack the columns and turn the vertical rule into a
         horizontal one above the button. */
      @media (max-width: 900px) {
        .national-controls-split {
          flex-wrap: wrap;
        }
        .national-control-action {
          flex: 1 1 100%;
          justify-content: flex-start;
          border-left: none;
          border-top: 1px solid #d8cdb8;

          padding-top: 1rem;
        }
        .national-control-field .form-group {
          margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
        }
      }

      /* Length + search controls: left-aligned with some spacing */
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_length,
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_filter {
        float: left;
        text-align: left;
        margin-right: 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
      }
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_filter label {
        white-space: nowrap;
      }

      /* DT Buttons download button */
      .dt-buttons {
        float: left;
        margin-right: 1rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
      }
      .dt-button {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 1rem !important;
        font-weight: 600 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        background: #6d1f2e !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #6d1f2e !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        padding: 4px 14px !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        line-height: 1.5 !important;
      }
      .dt-button:hover {
        background: #8b2737 !important;
        border-color: #8b2737 !important;
      }
      .dt-button:focus {
        outline: 3px solid #c9a84c !important;
        outline-offset: 2px !important;
      }

      /* ── National Data: card layout ───────────────────────────────────────── */

      /* Page header — warm beige background, maroon heading */
      .national-banner {
        background: #f9f7f4;
        border-bottom: 3px solid #e8e4db;
        padding: 1rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0;
      }
      .national-banner h1 {
        color: #6d1f2e;
        font-size: 2.6rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-bottom: 0.2rem;
      }
      .national-banner .national-intro {
        color: #2c2c2c;
        margin-top: 0;
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }

      /* Base card */
      .national-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-radius: 8px;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem 1.5rem 1.5rem;

      }

      /* Maroon accent on top edge of each card */
      .national-controls-card,
      .national-map-card,
      .national-table-card {
        border-top: 4px solid #6d1f2e;
      }

      /* Topic summary band: its own space between the controls and the map.
         Kept lighter than the other cards (gold left rule, no maroon top bar,

      .national-summary-card {
        background: #fbf8f2;

        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 19px;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #6d1f2e;
        margin: 0 0 0.4rem 0;
        line-height: 1.3;
      }

      /* Sort arrow contrast: DataTables sets opacity:0.125 on ::before/::after;
         using table.dataTable.table_national gives higher specificity than
         DataTables own selectors so !important is not needed on most rules.
         Partial opacity was the reason the arrows read as grey: white at 0.6
         over the slate header resolves to a mid grey. Every arrow is now solid
         white at full opacity, and the active sort direction is picked out in
         gold so the sorted state is still obvious. */
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc {
        background-image: none !important;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting::after,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::after,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::after {
        opacity: 1 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        font-size: 14px !important;
        line-height: 11px !important;
        right: 9px !important;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::after {
        color: #f2c75c !important;   /* gold: active direction, 8.7:1 on slate */
      }
    "))
  ),

  tags$main(
    role = "main",

    # ── Page header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-banner",
      h1("National Data"),
      tags$p(
        class = "national-intro",
        "To explore the data first select a category and then a topic. You can navigate the boxes below using the mouse or keyboard."
      )
    ),

    # ── Controls card ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-controls-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "Data selection controls",
        # Single horizontal row: the two selectors on the left, the download on
        # the right behind a vertical rule. The topic summary is no longer part
        # of this card; it sits in its own card below. Stacks under 900px.
        div(
          class = "national-controls-split",
          div(
            class = "national-controls-row",
            div(
              class = "national-control-field",
              selectInput(
                inputId = "national_category_selector",
                label   = "Select a category",
                choices = c(
                  "Demographics",
                  "Community Living",
                  "Community Participation",
                  "Work/Economic"
                ),
                selected = "Demographics"
              )
            ),
            div(
              class = "national-control-field",
              selectInput(
                inputId  = "national_variable_selector",
                label    = "Select a topic",
                choices  = .initial_nat_choices,
                selected = .initial_nat_selected
              )
            )
          ),
          tags$section(
            `aria-label` = "Download the selected topic",
            class = "national-control-action",
            downloadButton(
              "download_national_topic",
              "Download Selected Topic",
              class        = "btn-download-national",
              icon         = dl_icon(),
              `aria-label` = "Download the selected topic as an accessible, print-ready ADA-PARC report: map and key on page one, full data table on page two"
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Topic summary card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Given its own full-width band between the controls and the map so the
    # definition/high-low sentence reads as prose rather than as a caption
    # squeezed beside the controls.
    div(
      class = "national-card national-summary-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-labelledby` = "national-summary-heading",
        h2(
          "About This Topic",
          id    = "national-summary-heading",
          class = "national-summary-heading"
        ),
        div(
          `aria-live` = "polite",
          uiOutput("national_map_summary") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Map card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-map-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "Selected topic title",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_map_title") %>% withSpinner()
      ),
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "How to read the map",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_map_note")
      ),
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "State-by-state map of selected topic",
        div(
          id           = "national_map_img",
          role         = "img",
          `aria-label` = "Map of the United States. Use the topic dropdown to select a variable.",
          girafeOutput("national_ggmap", width = "100%", height = "400px") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # Tiny JS handler: updates the map div's aria-label reactively
    tags$script(HTML("
      Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('updateMapAriaLabel', function(x) {
        var el = document.getElementById('national_map_img');
        if (el) el.setAttribute('aria-label', x.label);
      });
    ")),

    # ── Table card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-table-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "Data table for selected topic",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_table_title"),
        div(
          class = "table-container",
          uiOutput("national_table") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Source note ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    tags$section(
      `aria-label` = "Data source",
      `aria-live` = "polite",
      uiOutput("national_source_note")
    )
    # NOTE: the "Download Selected Topic" button previously lived here at the
    # foot of the page. It now sits in the controls card, to the right of the
    # category and topic selectors.
  )
  , adaparc_footer
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Flag to control rendering
  ready_to_render <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

  national_category_selected <- reactive({
    switch(
      input$national_category_selector %||% "Demographics",
      "Demographics"            = "is_demographics",
      "Community Participation" = "is_community_participation",
      "Community Living"        = "is_community_living",
      "Work/Economic"           = "is_work_economic"
    )
  })

  national_variable_choices <- reactive({
    tibble::deframe(
      dict_vars %>%
        filter(
          !!sym(national_category_selected()) == TRUE,
          !is.na(national_dropdown_label)
        ) %>%
        select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable)
    )
  })

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Pre-populate the topic selector BEFORE the first reactive flush so the
  # map + table render with defaults on initial page load (without the
  # user having to change a dropdown). Uses freezeReactiveValue so
  # downstream reactives don't see a transient NULL/"" during the
  # selectize rebuild.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  observe({
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "national_variable_selector")
    cat_col <- national_category_selected()
    init_choices <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(!!sym(cat_col) == TRUE, !is.na(national_dropdown_label)) %>%
      select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable) %>%
      tibble::deframe() %>%
      names()
    init_default <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% init_choices) {
      "People with Disabilities"
    } else {
      init_choices[1]
    }
    updateSelectInput(
      session,
      "national_variable_selector",
      choices  = init_choices,
      selected = init_default
    )
  }, priority = 1000)

  # When both selectors have values, allow rendering
  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$national_category_selector) &&
        !is.null(input$national_variable_selector) &&
        nzchar(input$national_variable_selector)) {
      ready_to_render(TRUE)
    }
  })

  national_variable_selected <- reactive({
    req(national_category_selected())
    choices <- national_variable_choices()
    # If the select has not yet echoed its updated value back to the server,
    # fall back to the default so the table/map still render on first paint.
    current <- input$national_variable_selector
    if (is.null(current) || !nzchar(current) || !(current %in% names(choices))) {
      current <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% names(choices)) {
        "People with Disabilities"
      } else {
        names(choices)[1]
      }
    }
    req(current)
    choices[[current]]
  })

  # Reactively update the map image's aria-label whenever the topic changes,
  # so screen readers announce which variable is currently shown on the map.
  #
  # AUDITED FOR THE STARTUP MESSAGE RACE. Phase 1.4 of
  # docs/palette-v2-build-plan.qmd, 2026-08-03. This observe() fires on the
  # session's first flush, so it sends during startup exactly as the display
  # panel's push did. It is NOT exposed to the same defect, for two independent
  # reasons, and both are properties of where the handler lives rather than
  # luck:
  #
  #   1. The handler is a tags$script in this app's own UI, a few lines below.
  #      It is registered while the browser parses the document body, which is
  #      finished before shiny.js opens the websocket, which is in turn before
  #      the server can flush anything back. Nothing can arrive first. The
  #      display panel's handler is in www/cssloaders.html, injected into the
  #      HEAD ahead of Shiny's own dependencies, so it runs at a point where
  #      `window.Shiny` may not exist yet and registration has to be deferred.
  #      That deferral is the race.
  #
  #   2. If a message were dropped anyway, the div carries a static aria-label
  #      in the markup and the next topic change re-sends. The failure would be
  #      a stale but valid label, not an unusable control.
  #
  # These are the only two sendCustomMessage call sites in this file. If a
  # third is added, and its handler is not in the same document's body, give it
  # a client-initiated handshake like display_panel_ready rather than trusting
  # the ordering.
  observe({
    req(national_variable_selected())
    topic_label <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()
    category_label <- input$national_category_selector
    new_label <- paste0(
      "Choropleth map of the United States showing ", topic_label,
      " (", category_label, ") by state.",
      " Use the topic dropdown above to change the variable displayed."
    )
    session$sendCustomMessage("updateMapAriaLabel", list(label = new_label))
  })

  # ── Shared topic bundle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for the on-screen table AND the downloadable full
  # view. Building the friendly table, title, notes, and alt text here (rather
  # than separately in each output) guarantees the download always matches what
  # the user sees. Consumed by output$sortable_table and the download handler.
  national_topic_bundle <- reactive({
    req(ready_to_render())
    sel     <- national_variable_selected()
    req(sel)
    cat_col <- national_category_selected()

    var_row <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == sel) %>%
      head(1)

    title <- var_row %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    # Interpretation note: only for non-demographic, directional indicators.
    # Mirrors output$national_map_note so the download reads identically.
    is_demo <- isTRUE(var_row %>% pull(is_demographics))
    coding  <- var_row %>% pull(var_coding)
    interp_note <- ""
    if (!(is_demo || is.na(coding) || !(coding %in% c("pos", "neg")))) {
      # The colour reading holds for every series on these maps, not only the
      # disability series, so the note stays neutral on disability status.
      lead <- "Darker colors = more opportunity, lighter color = more disparity. "
      direction <- if (coding == "pos") {
        paste0("'", title, "' is a 'positive' indicator, meaning higher values indicate more opportunity.")
      } else {
        paste0("'", title, "' is a 'negative' indicator, meaning higher values indicate less opportunity.")
      }
      interp_note <- paste0(lead, direction)
    }

    # Source note (mirrors output$national_source_note)
    source_text <- var_row %>% pull(data_source_label)
    if (length(source_text) == 0 || is.na(source_text) || !nzchar(trimws(source_text))) {
      source_text <- "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
    }

    # Friendly table (mirrors former inline logic in output$sortable_table)
    national_vars_in_topic <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(
        (!!sym(cat_col)) == TRUE,
        var_topic == (dict_vars %>%
                        filter(
                          (!!sym(cat_col)) == TRUE &
                            var_readable == sel
                        ) %>%
                        pull(var_topic)),
        display == TRUE
      ) %>%
      select(var_pretty, var_readable)

    table_df <- national_data %>%
      mutate("State" = NAME) %>%
      arrange(State != "United States", State) %>%
      select(any_of(c("State", national_vars_in_topic %>% pull(var_readable)))) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          c(starts_with("pct_"), ends_with("_pct")),
          ~ scales::percent(.x, accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)
        ),
        across(
          where(is.numeric) & !starts_with("pct_") & !ends_with("_pct"),
          ~ scales::comma(.x, accuracy = 1)
        )
      ) %>%
      rename(!!!national_vars_in_topic %>% deframe())

    list(
      sel         = sel,
      title       = title,
      category    = input$national_category_selector %||% "",
      interp_note = interp_note,
      source_note = source_text,
      alt_text    = altText(national_data, sel),
      table_df    = table_df,
      vars        = national_vars_in_topic
    )
  })

  output$national_map_summary <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    HTML(
      sprintf(
        '<span class="map-summary">%s</span>',
        altText(national_data, national_variable_selected())
      )
    )
  })

  output$national_source_note <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    source_text <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(data_source_label)
    if (length(source_text) == 0 || is.na(source_text) || !nzchar(trimws(source_text))) {
      source_text <- "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
    }
    tags$p(
      class = "national-source-note",
      tags$strong("This indicator sourced from: "),
      source_text
    )
  })

  output$national_map_title <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    title <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()
    div(h2(title, class = "national-map-title"))
  })

  output$national_table_title <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    title <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    div(h2(title, class = "national-map-title"))
  })

  # Interpretation note shown in its own container ABOVE the map. The note
  # only applies to non-demographic indicators with an explicit pos/neg
  # direction. Coloring is now directional (dark = better outcome), so the
  # note explains that convention and names the indicator's direction.
  output$national_map_note <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    var_row <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1)

    is_demo <- isTRUE(var_row %>% pull(is_demographics))
    coding  <- var_row %>% pull(var_coding)

    title <- var_row %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    if (is_demo || is.na(coding) || !(coding %in% c("pos", "neg"))) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # Kept identical to the download copy above: the colour reading applies to
    # every series on the map, regardless of disability status.
    lead <- "Darker colors = more opportunity, lighter color = more disparity. "
    direction <- if (coding == "pos") {
      paste0("'", title, "' is a 'positive' indicator, meaning higher values indicate more opportunity.")
    } else {
      paste0("'", title, "' is a 'negative' indicator, meaning higher values indicate less opportunity.")
    }

    div(
      class = "map-interpretation-note",
      tags$span(class = "map-interpretation-note-label", "Interpretation Note: "),
      paste0(lead, direction)
    )
  })

  output$national_ggmap <- renderGirafe({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    gg <- render_national_map(
      national_variable_selected(),
      access_map_palette_selected(),
      na_color = access_map_na_selected()
    )
    girafe(
      ggobj      = gg,
      width_svg  = 10,
      height_svg = 5,
      options    = list(
        opts_tooltip(
          css = paste0(
            "background:#1c2b3a; color:white; ",
            "font-family:'EB Garamond',Georgia,serif; ",
            "font-size:15px; padding:8px 11px; border-radius:6px; ",
            "line-height:1.55; white-space:pre;"
          ),
          offx = 12, offy = -28, use_cursor_pos = TRUE
        ),
        # Deliberately sets stroke-WIDTH only, never stroke colour. Each state
        # now carries a border colour chosen from its own fill (near-black on
        # the light half of the ramp, white on the dark half; see the State
        # border ink notes in scripts/functions.R). Forcing a single navy on
        # hover, as this did before, overwrote that and left dark-filled states
        # with a 1.3:1 hover outline they could not show. Widening the state's
        # own ink keeps the hover affordance legible on every bin and in every
        # palette.
        opts_hover(css = "fill-opacity:0.75; stroke-width:2px;"),
        opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE, width = 1),
        opts_toolbar(saveaspng = FALSE),
        opts_selection(type = "none")
      )
    )
  })

  output$national_table <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    DT::dataTableOutput("sortable_table", width = "100%")
  })

  output$sortable_table <- DT::renderDataTable({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    # Table content comes from the shared bundle so it always matches the
    # downloadable full view (see national_topic_bundle above).
    bundle <- national_topic_bundle()
    national_data_table_friendly <- bundle$table_df

    all_columns      <- colnames(national_data_table_friendly)
    sortable_columns <- which(grepl("State|%", all_columns))

    # DataTables uses 0-based column indices; 0 is the State column
    non_state_columns <- setdiff(seq_along(all_columns) - 1, 0)

    # Per-table CSV export removed: downloading is now handled by the single
    # "Download Selected Topic" full-view button at the bottom of the page.
    DT::datatable(
      national_data_table_friendly,
      options = list(
        pageLength = -1,  # show all rows by default
        lengthMenu = list(
          c(10, 25, 50, -1),
          c("10", "25", "50", "All")
        ),
        scrollX   = TRUE,
        autoWidth = FALSE,
        columnDefs = list(
          # Make some columns unsortable
          list(
            targets   = setdiff(seq_along(all_columns) - 1, sortable_columns - 1),
            orderable = FALSE
          ),
          # Right-align all non-State columns
          list(
            targets   = non_state_columns,
            className = 'dt-right'
          )
        ),
        dom     = "lfrtip"  # length, filter, table, info, paging (no Buttons)
      ),
      rownames = FALSE,
      width    = "100%",
      # "compact" dropped: its 4px cell padding fought the roomier row
      # heights set in the national table CSS above.
      class    = "display table_national"
    )
  }, server = FALSE)

  # ── Download Selected Topic: full branded HTML view ─────────────────────────
  # Renders national_topic.qmd for the current selection into a self-contained,
  # ADA-PARC branded HTML: page 1 (banner, title, map + key, notes), page 2
  # (data table). All content is prepared here and passed via an RDS bundle so
  # the download always matches the on-screen view.
  nd_app_root <- normalizePath(
    getOption("shiny.appdir", default = getwd()),
    mustWork = FALSE
  )
  national_dir  <- file.path(nd_app_root, "national")
  national_qmd  <- file.path(national_dir, "national_topic.qmd")
  nd_out_dir    <- file.path(tempdir(), "ada_parc_national_dl")
  dir.create(nd_out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  output$download_national_topic <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      bundle <- national_topic_bundle()
      slug   <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", bundle$title)
      slug   <- gsub("^_|_$", "", slug)
      paste0("ADA-PARC_", slug, "_2024.html")
    },
    content = function(file) {
      withProgress(
        message = "Building your ADA-PARC report…",
        detail  = "This usually takes 15–25 seconds.",
        value   = 0.2,
        {
          bundle <- national_topic_bundle()

          # Render the map (ggplot from render_national_map) to an inline SVG
          # string. svglite emits the requested font-family; the browser pairs
          # it with the EB Garamond webfont loaded via font-loader.html.
          gg <- render_national_map(
            bundle$sel,
            access_map_palette_selected(),
            na_color = access_map_na_selected()
          )
          svg_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
          ggplot2::ggsave(
            filename = svg_tmp, plot = gg,
            device = svglite::svglite,
            width = 9, height = 6.4, bg = "white"
          )
          map_svg <- paste(readLines(svg_tmp, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
          unlink(svg_tmp)

          setProgress(0.45, detail = "Composing the document…")

          out_bundle <- list(
            title       = bundle$title,
            category    = bundle$category,
            interp_note = bundle$interp_note,
            source_note = bundle$source_note,
            alt_text    = bundle$alt_text,
            table_df    = bundle$table_df,
            map_svg     = map_svg,
            generated   = format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")
          )
          bundle_path <- file.path(nd_out_dir, "bundle.rds")
          saveRDS(out_bundle, bundle_path)

          setProgress(0.6, detail = "Rendering HTML…")

          tryCatch({
            quarto::quarto_render(
              input          = national_qmd,
              execute_params = list(bundle = bundle_path),
              execute_dir    = national_dir
            )
            rendered <- file.path(national_dir, "national_topic.html")
            if (file.exists(rendered)) {
              file.copy(rendered, file, overwrite = TRUE)
            } else {
              writeLines("<html><body>Report could not be generated.</body></html>", file)
            }
            setProgress(1)
          }, error = function(e) {
            showNotification(
              ui       = paste("Download failed:", conditionMessage(e)),
              type     = "error",
              duration = 15
            )
            writeLines(
              paste0("<html><body>Report could not be generated: ",
                     htmltools::htmlEscape(conditionMessage(e)), "</body></html>"),
              file
            )
          })
        }
      )
    }
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

# City Data

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(leaflet.extras2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(shinycssloaders)

# ----------------------------
# State choices
# ----------------------------
state_choices <- tibble::tibble(NAME = state.name, ABB = state.abb) %>%
  add_row(NAME = c("District of Columbia", "Puerto Rico"), ABB = c("DC", "PR")) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

# ----------------------------
# Helpers (ALL pct cols are dbl on 0–100 scale)
# ----------------------------
fmt_pct_1dp <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.1))
}

fmt_num <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", scales::comma(x, accuracy = 1))
}

create_number_percent_string <- function(num, pct) {
  paste0(fmt_num(num), " (", fmt_pct_1dp(pct), ")")
}

# Dollar formatter for ACS median earnings (B18140).
#
# ACS reports a median that falls in the top or bottom interval as the
# bound itself, so the raw values 250001 and 2499 are not real medians and
# must not be printed as though they were. Across the 8,407 places, 6 are
# top-coded and 40 are bottom-coded.
fmt_dollar <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x)    ~ "Not available",
    x >= 250001 ~ "$250,000 or more",
    x <= 2499   ~ "$2,500 or less",
    TRUE        ~ scales::dollar(x, accuracy = 1)
  )
}

# As above, but collapses to a plain-language phrase when the percentage is
# suppressed, so the reader sees "Not available" rather than "NA (NA)".
# Used for indicators that are genuinely missing for some places: health
# insurance (a handful of places) and anything sourced from ACS S1811,
# which resolves for only 694 of 8,407 places.
create_number_percent_string_or_na <- function(num, pct) {
  ifelse(is.na(as.numeric(pct)), "Not available",
         paste0(fmt_num(num), " (", fmt_pct_1dp(pct), ")"))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paired with/without-disability comparison tables (City Data tab)
#
# Every outcome indicator on the city page has a without-disability
# counterpart in city_place_full.Rds, at equal or better coverage. These two
# helpers render a pair as an accessible two-column table rather than as a
# bullet list, because a bullet carrying two values reads as a run-on
# sentence and gives screen reader users no column context.
#
# The PWD-to-PWOD column pairs MUST be declared explicitly. The naming is not
# consistent and cannot be derived: unemployment is
# pct_cni_18to64_nodis_unemployed, with "nodis" before the measure, while its
# neighbour is pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis with "nodis" after, and the
# health insurance columns put "nodis" in the middle. A
# paste0(var, "_nodis") would fail silently on several of them.
#
# cmp_row() builds one row spec. kind = "count_pct" formats as
# "12,345 (12.3%)"; kind = "dollar" formats a single ACS median with the
# top-code and bottom-code guards in fmt_dollar().
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cmp_row <- function(label, dis, nodis, kind = "count_pct", dis_pop = NA_character_,
                    nodis_pop = NA_character_) {
  list(label = label, dis = dis, nodis = nodis, kind = kind,
       dis_pop = dis_pop, nodis_pop = nodis_pop)
}

render_comparison_table <- function(row, rows, caption) {
  cell <- function(pct_col, pop_col, kind) {
    if (identical(kind, "dollar")) {
      fmt_dollar(row[[pct_col]])
    } else {
      create_number_percent_string_or_na(row[[pop_col]], row[[pct_col]])
    }
  }

  body <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    paste0(
      "<tr><th scope=\"row\">", r$label, "</th>",
      "<td>", cell(r$dis,   r$dis_pop,   r$kind), "</td>",
      "<td>", cell(r$nodis, r$nodis_pop, r$kind), "</td></tr>"
    )
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<table class=\"city-compare\">",
    "<caption>", caption, "</caption>",
    "<thead><tr>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">Indicator</th>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">With disability</th>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">Without disability</th>",
    "</tr></thead><tbody>",
    paste0(body, collapse = ""),
    "</tbody></table>"
  )
}

# Join-proof tract GEOID normalization (NO percent conversion)
normalize_tract_geoid <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", x)                   # digits only
  ifelse(nchar(x) >= 11, substr(x, nchar(x) - 10, nchar(x)), x)  # last 11 digits
}

ui <- fluidPage(

    tags$style(HTML("

      /* inherit www/styles.css from the parent flexdashboard.               */
      @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=EB+Garamond:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;0,800;1,400&display=swap');

      /* Universal font rule — covers Bootstrap resets and dynamic widgets */

      }

      body {

      }

      /* Page header banner */

      }

      .city-note-footer {
        max-width: none;
        margin-top: 1rem;
      }

      /* Section cards */

      }

      }

      .city-controls-card .shiny-input-container label {

        font-weight: 500;
      }
      .city-controls-card select.form-control,

        color: #1c2b3a !important;
      }

        font-size: 17px !important;
        color: #1c2b3a !important;

      .city-summary h4,
      .city-summary p,
      .city-summary ul,
      .city-summary li,

        color: #1c1c1c;
      }

        font-weight: 700;

        font-weight: 700;

      }
      /* Sub-headings inside a summary card: Race / Ethnicity, Sex, Ages 19
         to 64, and so on. The two descendant selectors below were written
         for an older markup where the b element sat inside a nested div;
         in the current markup the b element is a direct child of
         .city-summary, so neither matched and sub-headings were rendering
         at inherited body size, smaller than the 1.5rem list items they
         label. The direct-child selector is the one that actually applies.
         The other two are kept in case that markup returns. */
      .city-summary > b,
      .city-summary > div > b,
      .city-summary .city-age-item > b,
      .city-summary .col-md-12 > b {
        display: inline-block;
        font-size: 1.55rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-top: 0.75rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.35rem;

        letter-spacing: 0.01em;
      }

        line-height: 1.8;

        margin-bottom: 1rem;
        padding-left: 1.5rem;
      }

        margin-bottom: 0.45rem;
        padding-left: 0.1rem;
      }
      .city-summary .city-summary-help {
        font-size: 1.4rem;
        font-style: normal;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        margin-top: -0.1rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.85rem;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }

      /* Paired with/without-disability comparison tables.
         Semantic tables rather than bullet lists: column and row headers are
         announced by screen readers, and tabular figures keep the two value
         columns aligned so the comparison is readable at a glance. */
      .city-summary table.city-compare {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1.1rem;
        font-size: 1.4rem;
        line-height: 1.5;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare caption {
        text-align: left;
        font-weight: 700;
        font-size: 1.45rem;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        padding: 0 0 0.3rem;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare th,
      .city-summary table.city-compare td {
        border: 1px solid #ded8cf;
        padding: 0.4rem 0.55rem;
        text-align: left;
        vertical-align: top;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare thead th {
        background: #6b0f0f;
        color: #ffffff;
        font-weight: 600;
        border-color: #6b0f0f;
        font-size: 1.3rem;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] {
        background: #f6f2ec;
        font-weight: 600;
        width: 42%;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare tbody tr:nth-child(even) td {
        background: #fbf9f6;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare td {
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      /* Narrow screens: allow the value columns to wrap rather than forcing a
         horizontal scroll inside the card. */
      @media (max-width: 62em) {
        .city-summary table.city-compare td { white-space: normal; }
        .city-summary table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] { width: 38%; }
      }
      /* With the card-level h3 headings removed, the first sub-section
         heading sits flush at the top of each card rather than carrying
         the inter-section spacing meant to separate blocks. */
      .city-summary h4:first-child {
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
      }

      /* Equal-height card rows.
         Bootstrap 3 lays .row out with floats, so two cards side by side end
         at their own natural heights and the shorter one leaves a ragged
         edge. Making just these rows flex containers equalises the cards.
         flex-wrap keeps the single-column stack on narrow screens, and the
         negative gutter margins BS3 puts on .row still apply. Scoped to this
         class so no other row on the site is affected. */
      .city-summary-row {
        display: flex;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
      }
      .city-summary-row > [class*='col-'] {
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
      }
      .city-summary-row > [class*='col-'] > .city-summary {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
      }

      /* Full-width demographics card (row two).
         Holds both Disability Demographics and Disability Types. Everything
         inside stacks in a single vertical column at every width. An earlier
         version flowed the longer lists into two CSS columns to use the extra
         width, but two columns of bullets read worse than one, so the lists
         run straight down and the card simply ends where its content ends. */
      .city-summary-wide .city-age-item > ul {
        margin-bottom: 0.35rem;
      }

      /* Full-width explanatory card, used for the Community Living domain,
         which has no city-level indicators available yet. Lighter treatment
         than a data card so it does not read as though data is missing. */
      .city-summary-note {
        background: #faf8f5;
        border-top-width: 3px;
      }
      .city-summary-note h4:first-child {
        margin-top: 0.25rem;

      /* Shared heading above both summary columns. Mirrors .city-summary
         h3 and p, but sits outside the cards so it can span the full

      .city-summary-header {
        text-align: center;

      .city-summary-header h3 {

        color: #6b0f0f;
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;

        margin: 0 auto;
        max-width: 90ch;
      }

      /* ── Select inputs: font, sizing, and maroon accent on focus ──────── */
      .control-label {
        font-size: 20px !important;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #6b0f0f;
        margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
      }
      .selectize-input,
      .selectize-dropdown,
      .selectize-dropdown-content,
      .selectize-input input,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .active {
        font-size: 19px !important;
      }
      .selectize-input {
        border: 1.5px solid #c8b8b8 !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        background: #fff !important;
        color: #1c1c1c !important;
        padding: 7px 10px !important;

      .selectize-input.focus,

      .selectize-dropdown {
        border: 1.5px solid #c8b8b8 !important;

      }
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option:hover,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option.active,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .selected {

      /* ── Leaflet legend ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
```
