# ── Glossary data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Definitions for terms mapped to a variable are pulled from dict_vars
# (national_summary_text) so the glossary stays in sync with the data
# dictionary. Terms with no matching variable use a plain-language fallback.
gloss_def <- function(key, fallback = NA_character_) {
  v <- dict_vars %>%
    filter(var_readable == key, !is.na(national_summary_text)) %>%
    head(1) %>%
    pull(national_summary_text)
  if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v) || !nzchar(trimws(v))) fallback else trimws(v)
}

glossary_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Term = c(
    "PWD (People with Disabilities)",
    "CNI (Civilian Noninstitutional Population)",
    "Group Quarters",
    "Nursing Home (Institutional Group Quarters)",
    "Non-Institutional (Community)",
    "HCBS (Home and Community-Based Services)",
    "ACS Five-Year Estimates",
    "Community Living",
    "Community Participation",
    "Work and Economic"
  ),
  Definition = c(
    gloss_def("pct_cni_total_dis"),
    gloss_def("pop_cni_total_all"),
    gloss_def(
      "pop_grpquarters",
      paste(
        "Group quarters are places where people live or stay in a group",
        "living arrangement that is owned or managed by an organization",
        "providing housing or services. The Census Bureau divides them into",
        "institutional settings (such as nursing homes and correctional",
        "facilities) and non-institutional settings (such as group homes,",
        "shelters, and college housing)."
      )
    ),
    gloss_def("pop_grp_instgroupquarters_total_dis"),
    gloss_def("pct_grp_dis_noninstgroupquarters"),
    paste(
      "Home and Community-Based Services are Medicaid-funded supports that",
      "help people with disabilities and older adults live in their own",
      "homes and communities instead of in institutions such as nursing",
      "homes. They can include personal care, in-home assistance, and day",
      "programs."
    ),
    paste(
      "The American Community Survey (ACS) is an ongoing U.S. Census Bureau",
      "survey. Five-year estimates combine data collected over 60 months,",
      "which produces more reliable statistics for small populations and",
      "geographies than single-year estimates, though the figures are less",
      "current."
    ),
    paste(
      "One of the three ADA-PARC outcome domains. It measures whether people",
      "with disabilities live in the community, at home or in community-based",
      "settings, rather than in institutions such as nursing homes or",
      "correctional facilities."
    ),
    paste(
      "One of the three ADA-PARC outcome domains. It measures access to",
      "community life for people with disabilities, including transportation,",
      "education, health insurance, and access to technology."
    ),
    paste(
      "One of the three ADA-PARC outcome domains. It measures economic",
      "outcomes for people with disabilities, including employment, income,",
      "poverty, and housing affordability."
    )
  )
)

glossary_dl <- tags$dl(
  class = "glossary-list",
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(glossary_df)), function(i) {
    tagList(
      tags$dt(glossary_df$Term[i]),
      tags$dd(glossary_df$Definition[i])
    )
  })
)

# Help page content
div(class = "help-wrap",

  # Page title
  div(class = "help-banner",
    tags$h1("Help", class = "help-heading"),
    tags$p("Resources and settings for the ADA-PARC Data Tool.", class = "help-subheading")
  ),

  # Map settings card
  div(class = "help-card",
    tags$p(class = "help-card-title", "Map Display Settings"),
    # Palette choices come from ADAPARC_PALETTES in scripts/palettes.R. No hex is
    # inlined here, and no ColorBrewer name is used: every option is an explicit
    # four-stop ramp that has been measured against the admission criteria in
    # that file (adjacent-bin separation of at least 15 CIEDE2000 under normal
    # vision and under simulated protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia).
    #
    # The six non-brand options that shipped before this (Purple Gradient,
    # Yellow-Orange, Yellow-Orange-Red, Grayscale Gradient, Teal-Blue Gradient,
    # Green-Yellow Gradient) were retired on 2026-07-30; each either failed or
    # sat marginal against that floor. See docs/color-palette-expansion.qmd.
    #
    # `choices` is a named vector of label -> id, so input$access_map_palette
    # carries the STABLE id ("heritage") rather than the display label. Renaming
    # a palette in the UI therefore cannot break the reactive below.
    selectInput(
      inputId  = "access_map_palette",
      label    = "Select Map Color Palette:",
      choices  = map_palette_choices(),
      selected = PALETTE_DEFAULT
    ),
    tags$p(class = "help-palette-note",
      "Your selected palette applies to maps in national data and city data, and is a visual preference only. It does not change how the maps are read: on national maps, darker colors always mean more opportunity and lighter colors mean more disparity, whichever palette you choose."
    ),
    # Plain-language description of the palette currently selected, so the
    # reason to pick one over another is visible at the point of choice rather
    # than buried in documentation.
    uiOutput("access_map_palette_note"),
    tags$p(class = "help-palette-note",
      "Scorecards and fact sheets always use the ADA-PARC palette and are not affected by this setting."
    ),
    # The Display button is available on every page. This dropdown is kept in
    # step with it, and stays here because Help is where the explanation of the
    # palettes lives; the panel is where a reader looking at a map wants the
    # control. Neither is authoritative; both write through
    # set_display_settings(). High contrast has no copy here because it needs
    # no explanation, only a switch.
    tags$p(class = "help-palette-note",
      "You can also change this without leaving a map: use the ",
      tags$strong("Display"),
      " button in the bottom right corner of any page, which also carries the high contrast setting."
    )
  ),

  # Glossary card
  div(class = "help-card",
    tags$p(class = "help-card-title", "Glossary"),
    tags$p(
      "Plain-language definitions for terms used throughout the ADA-PARC Data Tool. Download the full glossary as a CSV file."
    ),
    glossary_dl,
    downloadButton("download_glossary", "Download Glossary (CSV)",
                   class = "btn-glossary-download", icon = dl_icon(),
                   `aria-label` = "Download glossary of terms as a CSV file")
  ),

  # Contact note
  tags$p(
    "For questions about the data, methodology, or site functionality, please reach out to our team.",
    class = "help-palette-note",
    style = "margin-top: 1.5rem;"
  ),
  tags$a(
    href  = "mailto:joyhammel@uic.edu",
    class = "email-button",
    "Contact Us"

)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DISPLAY SETTINGS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# One source for the two reader-facing display choices, palette and contrast.
# Phase 2 of docs/palette-v1-build-plan.qmd, added 2026-08-03.
#
# WHY NOT JUST READ input$access_map_palette. From phase 3 there are two
# controls bound to the same setting: this Help page dropdown and the floating
# Display panel reachable from every tab. Two inputs cannot both be "the"
# setting. Everything downstream reads display_settings() instead, so adding a
# third control later is one more observer and no change anywhere else.
#
# SESSION SCOPE, AND WHY IT MATTERS HERE. These are per-session reactives,
# deliberately not globals. scripts/palettes.R is sourced into the global
# environment, which is correct for constants, but a display setting held there
# would be shared by every visitor to the deployed app, and two readers would
# fight over each other's palette.

display_state <- reactiveValues(
  palette           = PALETTE_DEFAULT,
  contrast          = CONTRAST_DEFAULT,
  # TRUE once the URL has been read and found to carry an explicit ?contrast=.
  # Only the prefers-contrast observer reads it, to know whether to stand down.
  contrast_from_url = FALSE
)

# The single source. Every consumer reads from here, never from an input id.
display_settings <- reactive({
  list(
    palette  = pal_id(display_state$palette),
    contrast = pal_contrast_mode(display_state$contrast)
  )
})

# Write a setting, keep every bound control in step, and mirror it into the URL
# so a reader can bookmark or share the view they configured.
#
# mode = "replace" rather than "push": changing palette three times should not
# put three entries in the reader's back button.
#
# The early return on "nothing changed" is what stops the loop between this and
# the dropdown observer below, which fires again when updateSelectInput lands.
set_display_settings <- function(palette = NULL, contrast = NULL,
                                 announce = TRUE) {
  changed <- character(0)

  if (!is.null(palette)) {
    p <- pal_id(palette)
    if (!identical(p, display_state$palette)) {
      display_state$palette <- p
      changed <- c(changed, "palette")
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(contrast)) {
    k <- pal_contrast_mode(contrast)
    if (!identical(k, display_state$contrast)) {
      display_state$contrast <- k
      changed <- c(changed, "contrast")
    }
  }
  if (!length(changed)) return(invisible(FALSE))

  updateSelectInput(
    session  = getDefaultReactiveDomain(),
    inputId  = "access_map_palette",
    selected = display_state$palette
  )
  updateQueryString(
    paste0("?palette=",   display_state$palette,
           "&contrast=",  display_state$contrast),
    mode = "replace"
  )
  push_display_panel(announce = if (announce) changed else character(0))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Push the FULL state to the floating Display panel in www/cssloaders.html.
#
# Full state, never a delta, so the panel and the Help page dropdown cannot
# drift apart: whatever R believes is what both controls show. The choices list
# travels with it so the panel's <option> list is built from
# map_palette_choices() rather than being a second hardcoded list of palettes.
#
# `announce` names which settings changed. The panel drops the sentence into an
# aria-live region, so a screen reader user learns the setting took effect; a
# sighted reader sees the map recolour, and this is the equivalent.
push_display_panel <- function(announce = character(0)) {
  sess <- getDefaultReactiveDomain()
  if (is.null(sess)) return(invisible(FALSE))

  choices <- map_palette_choices()      # label -> id
  ids     <- unname(choices)
  labels  <- names(choices)
  pal_lab <- labels[match(display_state$palette, ids)]
  high    <- identical(display_state$contrast, "high")

  said <- character(0)
  if ("palette" %in% announce) {
    said <- c(said, paste0("Map color palette set to ", pal_lab, "."))
  }
  if ("contrast" %in% announce) {
    said <- c(said, if (high)
      "High contrast turned on." else "High contrast turned off.")
  }

  # Say plainly that high contrast has taken the palette over. Without this the
  # selector reads "Cividis" while the map is black and white, which looks like
  # a bug rather than a setting.
  note <- map_palette_note(display_state$palette)
  if (high) {
    note <- paste(note,
                  "High contrast is on, so maps are currently drawn in High",
                  "Contrast Mono. Turning it off restores this palette.")
  }

  # Empty string, not NULL, for `announce`. A NULL in an R list serialises to a
  # JSON empty object, which is TRUTHY in JavaScript, and the live region would
  # end up announcing "[object Object]".
  sess$sendCustomMessage("adaparcDisplaySync", list(
    choices  = lapply(seq_along(ids),
                      function(i) list(id = ids[i], label = labels[i])),
    palette  = display_state$palette,
    contrast = display_state$contrast,
    note     = note,
    announce = paste(said, collapse = " "),
    # Phase 4.3. The generated :root block travels with the state that produced
    # it, in the same message, so the tokens and the data-adaparc-contrast hook
    # in www/styles.css cannot end up describing different modes. This is why
    # it is not a separate shinyjs::runjs() call: two channels would be two
    # chances to arrive out of order.
    css      = pal_css_rules(display_state$palette, display_state$contrast)
  ))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Read the settings out of the URL once, on load, so ?palette=cividis_r or
# ?contrast=high arrives already applied. Unknown or misspelled values are
# absorbed by pal_id() and pal_contrast_mode(); a wrong colour is recoverable
# and a blank map is not.
#
# The unconditional push at the end used to be what populated the panel on a
# cold load. It is now a belt-and-braces second chance rather than the
# mechanism, because it fires on the session's first flush and could beat the
# browser's registration of the 'adaparcDisplaySync' handler, in which case
# Shiny discards the message and the panel's select stays empty. The panel now
# asks for its own state; see the display_panel_ready observer below. This push
# is kept because when it does win the race it saves a round trip, and when it
# loses it costs nothing. Silent either way: nothing has changed from the
# reader's point of view, so there is nothing to announce.
observeEvent(TRUE, {
  sess <- getDefaultReactiveDomain()
  if (is.null(sess)) return()
  qs <- parseQueryString(sess$clientData$url_search)
  # Recorded so the operating-system preference below knows to stand down. An
  # explicit ?contrast= in the URL is the reader saying what they want for THIS
  # view, and it outranks a machine-wide default.
  display_state$contrast_from_url <- !is.null(qs$contrast)
  if (!is.null(qs$palette) || !is.null(qs$contrast)) {
    set_display_settings(palette = qs$palette, contrast = qs$contrast,
                         announce = FALSE)
  }
  push_display_panel()
}, once = TRUE)

# Phase 1.1 of docs/palette-v2-build-plan.qmd, 2026-08-03. The other half of
# the handshake. The floating panel sets this input once it has registered its
# custom message handler and the websocket is up; R replies with the full
# state, exactly as push_display_panel() sends it anywhere else.
#
# WHY THE ASK COMES FROM THE BROWSER. Shiny drops a custom message SILENTLY
# when nothing is listening for its name. Only the browser knows when it has
# finished listening, so only the browser can say when it is safe to send. The
# server cannot detect the failure and cannot retry on a condition it cannot
# observe.
#
# NOT once = TRUE. A reconnecting session re-registers the handler and asks
# again, and the panel would otherwise come back empty for the rest of the
# visit. push_display_panel() is idempotent, and the panel's applyState()
# rebuilds the option list only when it actually differs, so an extra push
# costs one message and disturbs nothing the reader is looking at.
#
# Silent. This is a delivery mechanism, not a setting change, and the live
# region should not announce a palette the reader did not choose.
observeEvent(input$display_panel_ready, {
  push_display_panel()
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

# 4.5. Honour `prefers-contrast: more` on a cold load, so a reader who has
# already configured their machine does not have to find the panel.
#
# WHY THIS COMES FROM THE BROWSER RATHER THAN A CSS MEDIA QUERY. A media query
# would restyle the chrome but leave the maps on the reader's chosen palette,
# because those are ggplot and leaflet fills chosen in R and baked into the
# output. The whole point of routing everything through display_settings() is
# that the two cannot disagree, so the preference is read once in JavaScript and
# applied as a setting like any other.
#
# Read ONCE, at connect, and never again. Watching the media query live would
# mean a reader who turns high contrast off in the panel gets it turned back on
# by their operating system, which is the machine overruling the person.
observeEvent(input$display_os_prefers_contrast, {
  if (isTRUE(display_state$contrast_from_url)) return()
  if (!isTRUE(input$display_os_prefers_contrast)) return()
  set_display_settings(contrast = "high", announce = FALSE)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE, once = TRUE)

# ── The two controls ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Both are CONTROLS over the setting, not the setting. Each one only ever calls
# set_display_settings(); neither reads the other, and neither is authoritative.
# Adding a third is one more observer here and no change anywhere else.
#
# ignoreInit on the Help dropdown so the first flush does not write a query
# string onto a URL the reader never touched. The panel inputs need no such
# guard, because they are only ever set from a real change event in the browser.
observeEvent(input$access_map_palette, {
  set_display_settings(palette = input$access_map_palette)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)

observeEvent(input$display_panel_palette, {
  set_display_settings(palette = input$display_panel_palette)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

observeEvent(input$display_panel_contrast, {
  set_display_settings(
    contrast = if (isTRUE(input$display_panel_contrast)) "high" else "standard"
  )
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE)


# ── Reactive palette selection ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Returns a colorRampPalette FUNCTION rather than a colour vector, because both
# consumers (render_national_map() in scripts/functions.R and city_map_colors()
# below) already branch on is.function(). Keeping that contract means this swap
# needed no change in either consumer.
#
# pal_effective_fill_id() is where high contrast overrides the reader's palette
# with High Contrast Mono. It lives in scripts/palettes.R and is the same helper
# pal_css_vars() calls, so the maps and the stylesheet cannot end up disagreeing
# about what high contrast means.
access_map_fill_id <- reactive({
  ds <- display_settings()
  pal_effective_fill_id(ds$palette, ds$contrast)
})

access_map_palette_selected <- reactive({
  colorRampPalette(pal_fill(4, access_map_fill_id()))
})

# No-data fill for the currently selected palette. Per-palette, not global:
# High Contrast Mono spans pure white to pure black, so the shared grey would be
# indistinguishable from its lightest band. See the NO-DATA note in palettes.R.
access_map_na_selected <- reactive({
  pal_na(access_map_fill_id())
})

# Description of the selected palette, shown under the dropdown. This reports
# what the READER CHOSE, not the effective fill, so a high contrast reader still
# sees the description of the palette they will get back when they turn it off.
output$access_map_palette_note <- renderUI({
  tags$p(class = "help-palette-note",
         tags$strong("About this palette: "),
         map_palette_note(display_settings()$palette))
})

# Glossary CSV download (content built from glossary_df, so the file
# always matches the definition list shown on the Help page).
output$download_glossary <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() "ADAPARC_Glossary.csv",
  content  = function(file) {
    readr::write_csv(glossary_df, file)
  }
)
